# Build a simple daily habit check-in with Siri and Apple Intelligence


Imagine your iPhone asking you one quick question every evening — "How many glasses of water did you drink today?" — and answering with a short, encouraging line. You can build exactly that in the Shortcuts app: a **shortcut** is a small set of steps the app runs for you, and Apple calls each step an **action**. One of those actions, **Use Model**, sends text to Apple Intelligence.

## Before you start
- An iPhone that supports Apple Intelligence, with Apple Intelligence turned on and the latest iOS installed. Apple keeps the list of supported models on its website, and notes that Apple Intelligence isn't available in all languages or regions and that usage limits may apply.
- The **Shortcuts** app — it comes with the iPhone; if you deleted it, it's free in the App Store.
- About **10 minutes**.
- One honest limit: this check-in doesn't keep a history or learn your routine. It asks, answers, and that's it.

The button and action names below come from Apple's Shortcuts User Guide. If your iPhone is set to another language, you'll see them translated.

## Step 1 — Create a new shortcut and name it
Open the **Shortcuts** app and tap the **Add** button (the plus sign). Tap **New Shortcut** at the top, tap **Rename**, type **Water Check**, and confirm. You'll say this name to Siri later, so keep it short. Apple warns that if a shortcut has the same name as a standard Siri command, Siri runs the shortcut instead — so avoid names like "What time is it".
You'll know it worked when the new name appears at the top of the empty shortcut.

💬 Example: name it `Water Check`.

## Step 2 — Ask the daily question
Tap **Add Action**, search for **Ask for Input**, and tap it. When the shortcut runs, this action opens a box with your question and passes your answer to the next action. Apple says it accepts words, dates or numbers, and the keyboard adapts to the type — so tap the answer type in the action and choose **Number**. Then tap the question text and type your own question.
You'll know it worked when the action shows your question and the answer type is set to Number.

💬 Example: type `How many glasses of water did you drink today?` as the question.

## Step 3 — Add a friendly reply from Apple Intelligence
Swipe up on the search field at the bottom of the screen, search for **Use Model**, tap it, and choose **On-Device** — Apple says it handles simple requests without needing a network connection. In the text field below **Use Model**, type the prompt below, then, at the very end, pick the answer from Step 2 from the suggestions above the keyboard (Shortcuts usually calls it **Provided Input**). Apple's guide confirms a prompt can include the output of a previous action.
You'll know it worked when the Use Model action shows your prompt with the answer from Step 2 at the end.

💬 Example: "In one short, friendly sentence, tell me how my day went and give me one easy tip for tomorrow. My goal is [your daily goal] glasses. Today I drank:"

## Step 4 — Test it in the app
Tap the play button at the bottom of the shortcut editor to run it. The question box opens; type a number and tap **Done**. A moment later Apple Intelligence answers with its short sentence. If the reply feels too long or too stern, edit the prompt — for example add "no more than 15 words" — and run it again.
You'll know it worked when you see a one-sentence reply that mentions your number.

## Step 5 — Run it with Siri
Tap **Done** to save the shortcut. From now on you can start it by voice: Apple's guide says to activate Siri and then say the name of a shortcut. Siri asks your question, you answer out loud, and you get the reply.
You'll know it worked when Siri asks your water question after you say the name.

💬 Example: say `Hey Siri, Water Check`.

## Step 6 — Get a daily reminder (optional)
To be asked every evening, add a **Time of Day** automation. In Apple's current guide: open the shortcut, tap **Edit**, then **Automation**, and choose a trigger such as **Time of Day** — for example 8:00 PM, repeating daily. (On older iOS versions this lives in the **Automation** tab of the Shortcuts app.) Apple notes that when the time comes, you get a notification asking you to run the automation — perfect here, because the shortcut needs your answer anyway.
You'll know it worked when a notification about your shortcut appears at the time you chose.

## Common mistakes
- **You can't find Use Model:** Apple Intelligence may be turned off, your iPhone may not support it, or it may not be available in your language or region yet. Steps 1, 2 and 5 still work without it.
- **The answer type is still text:** you'll get the full keyboard instead of the number pad. Set the Ask for Input answer type to Number.
- **Expecting a log:** this shortcut doesn't save your answers. It's a daily nudge, not a diary.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** One small question at the same time every day is often enough to keep a habit going — water, a short walk, a few minutes of reading.
- **For your business or work:** The same pattern works as an end-of-day check-in: "How many tasks did you finish today?" with a one-line reply.
- **If you're just getting started:** Build Steps 1–4 first and run the shortcut from the app. Add Siri and the daily reminder once you like the reply.

## Try it now
Open Shortcuts, tap **Add**, name the shortcut **Water Check**, add **Ask for Input** (set to Number) and **Use Model** with the prompt above, and tap the play button. You'll have your first daily check-in in about five minutes.
